patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` applied cleanly to the staged vulnerable checkout. On the original PoC, the fixed rebuild stays clean and the root-side assertion records `ref_cleanup_before_free=1` at the same `xmlTextReaderFreeProp()` cleanup site where the vulnerable run records `ref_cleanup_before_free=0` before reloading the stale attribute in `xmlValidateRef()`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project-code materialization of vulnerability-relevant attacker state. Once the witness DTD causes `xmlIsRef(...)` to classify the parsed `src@ref` attribute as a reference, this call consumes the attacker-controlled attribute value and the new `xmlAttr` pointer and starts building the `doc->refs` entry later walked by the validator.

The reader-side attribute cleanup removes ID-table state only. For a reference attribute, this function never performs the analogous `doc->refs` cleanup before the same `cur` object is later freed, so the `xmlRef` stored earlier still retains a dangling `xmlAttr *`.

Final crashing dereference. During end-of-document validation, `xmlValidateRef` takes the non-NULL-attribute path for the retained `xmlRef` entry and reads `attr->atype`; on the witness path that `attr` still points to an already-freed `xmlAttr`.

nodes.state: `xmlValidateRef()` reloads the released attribute pointer into local `attr` from the persisted reference entry instead of taking the name-only fallback path.
nodes.evidence: In the vulnerable trace, the `validate_ref_load` event records the same pointer value as the earlier released `cur` from `freeprop_guard`.
